And now if we can actually look at the report itself, which is P957. And if you go to paragraph 2 of that report. And if I think we need -- in fact if you -- I'm sorry. If we go to the bottom there, you will see it's the same episode. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you'll see that if you go to the final sentence of that paragraph, it reads: "The General reacted immediately by phoning the Minister of Internal Affairs and asking him to contact with the civil police in Split to establish coordination to avoid these accidents in the future. He told us that the officer will be punished." Now, do you see the difference between your statement and what you actually reported in the sense that Mr. Cermak had to call the Ministry of Internal Affairs who then had to call a police station get ECMM some relief?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could please go back to P1284 which is your statement from 1997, and that's tab 2 in your binder. And if we could please go to page 2 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: The next page, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you can go to the paragraph that begins: "During our meetings with General Cermak." And if you could please go to the second sentence which begins: "However, he was not able to control and guarantee our freedom of movement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: "He informed us at all times that we had necessary freedom of movement. However, meeting the police at check-points, especially in the southern area, we were severely restricted in our movement. Addressing this problem to General Cermak, he appeared to do his utmost to solve these problems. But it never impacted the police concerned, and we were still opposed by restriction of movement." Have you finished looking that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, that, you are referring to the Krajina generally when you make that statement. Yes?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But when you spoke with him, he was trying to sincerely help you, wasn't he, even though he was unable to influence these restrictions of movement upon you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any further questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Next one will be you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Hansen, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you could please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up P1283.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's your statement that you gave in 1995, Mr. Hansen. In that statement, in the last page, under section 6, you note that: "Soon after noon, the 5th of August," you're reference Knin, "we saw HV special police and military police."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Then at P1285, paragraph 7, which is your 2008 statement, you said that you left the UN camp for the first time on August 7th. My question to you is: How could you see the HV special police and military police on August 5 when you were not out of the camp until August 7th?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could see events taking place just outside the perimeter of the barracks and was quite -- quite many persons moving around just outside, and from our vantage point on a balcony inside the barracks, we could see activities outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. How do you know these were -- is there such a thing as HV special police?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is that something somebody told you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- today I have no additional comment to -- to the entry into the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is no such thing as HV special police?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You also note military police that you saw them on August 5th. How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have -- I have no additional comment to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you can't tell us how the special police or the military police or the Croatian military were dressed in any way, other than having a uniform on?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no recollection of this today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to state that you're guessing that there was something called the HV special police or someone told you that there was something like that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the information must come from somewhere, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that. But you have no source for that information; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today I cannot reveal any detailed source of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't give us any of that detail either in your earlier statement that you gave in December of 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I thought that was the December 1995 statement. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I was referring to both December of 1995 statement and the 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The same is true for both statements, Mr. Hansen; correct? You can't tell what the source was for your information that there was such a thing as HV special police or military police that you saw on August 5th?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's fair to state, is it not, Mr. Hansen, that you do not know or did not know at the time that you were in Sector South how the Croatian military was organised; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You cannot tell us at that time how the Croatian civil police was organised, correct, who was responsible to whom?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early days of the operation, I did not recall seeing any civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking in general, not just in the early days of the operation.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that you do not know how the Ministry of Interior special police was organised; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time you could not identify either -- either of those with any specificity by the kind of uniform they were wearing. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that the special police was not a part of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now your job as an ECMM monitor during the entire time you were in Sector South was to monitor, to observe. And you're telling me or you're telling us that the entire time you were in Sector South when you were monitoring and observing, you were unaware that the special police were a part of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I -- today I can only say that I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever ask anyone for a chart or a diagram or a schematic of any of the civilian military or police structures that were in place after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You're accusing in your reports certain people with uniforms on that you claim are either HV special police or police or military, yet you don't know how they're organised or to whom they belong?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it will be appreciated that there was a -- the situation was framed by -- by chaos, by vacuum. And in this kind of situation, you are not addressing questions like the organisation of a force to a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a fairly large territory, correct, Sector South?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it was very rugged territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time of Operation Storm as a member of the European Community Monitoring Mission that the special police for purposes of this operation were under the command of the Main Staff of the Croatian army in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was in overall command of the special police?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that at no time and under no circumstances were the Ministry of Interior special police ever in Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that at no time and under no circumstances were the special police ever in Obrovac, Benkovac, or Drnis?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever observe the Ministry of Interior special police in a mop-up operation anywhere in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the role was of the Ministry of Interior special police in conducting mop-up operations in Sector South after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you relied -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: For the Court's reference, since there are many references in Mr. Hansen's materials an exhibits that discuss either clean-up or mop-up operations in areas in which the special police were not, I'm just going to list by exhibit number the documents that set forth where the special police were and at what time, so the Court can have that reference rather than go through all those documents that Mr. Hansen doesn't know anything about. They are, in order, D543, D555, D550, P584, P583, D552, P585, D554, and P621.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I would just like to seek some clarification. Mr. Kuzmanovic stated that these were references in Mr. Hansen's materials an exhibits, yet those exhibit numbers I don't think were tendered through Mr. Hansen. So if they're general exhibits about ECMM reports, that's fine. I just want to clarify that for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I could spend, you know, 35 minutes going through all of Mr. Hansen's reports in which ge discusses where there were military or special police conducting mop-up operations and which they were not. And we would prefer to do that, I guess we can take the time to do that, but I'm just trying to make things a little more simpler, Your Honour. Excuse my obstruction of vision with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. I was simply asking whether the exhibits that Mr. Kuzmanovic were listing were Mr. Hansen's materials or not. I have no problems with him listing some of them, all of them, how many he wants. I just want the record to be clear as to what is being listed. That's all. I'm not trying to impede Mr. Kuzmanovic in his attempt to assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: None of those documents are ECMM documents. They are P documents or D documents that refer to things like the war diary of the Croatian -- Ministry of Interior special police, reports of the Ministry of Interior special police, places --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be very practical. It's -- it seems as if we are a bit the area of argument rather than in hearing testimony. Because what you say, Mr. Kuzmanovic, is where the witness, due to his lack of knowledge of the structural organisation, uniforms that were worn at the time, cannot assist us properly in identifying where the special police were, that you say that all these documents in which the presence of the military police appears should be compared, should at least be looked at before we come to any conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this is, of course, to some extent already concluding evaluating the, I would say the rather, well, negative in the sense of not being affirmative evidence by this witness. At the same time I do not hear Mr. Hedaraly complaining about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can use an example, Your Honour, just as an example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we take one example and just to know exactly what we are talking about, and if you do it briefly, Mr. Kuzmanovic, then we know exactly what you intend, what you expect us to do, and we have one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. We'll go to P1290, page 9. If it's page 9 of the document I'm -- it's page 9 of the document, not necessarily at the top it will say page 9. The last four digits are 1809 on the bottom page. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the paragraph that begins with: "Two houses were observed ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If Madam Registrar would please enlarge that, just toward the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, this document states in part: "Two houses were observed burning on the Drnis-Knin road at midday, 2 September. That night, a major blaze occurred in a neighbourhood of Knin at about 2100 hours. UNMOs and other personnel who went to investigate were turned back by special police, who were driving the other way. They said a restriction of movement had been implemented effective 200 hours." Now, Mr. Hansen, 1290 was part of your comprehensive survey report, this particular section, on the consequences of Operation Storm. Now, it's fair to state that you did not observe the special police in this section of the report; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you were not aware that there were no special police on the Drnis-Knin road, at least according to any documents that I have previously cited, on 2nd of September? You have no personal knowledge after that; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, Mr. Hansen, of P1283, which was your 1995 statement, which I had referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could pull that up, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The last page of that document, the third sentence, fourth sentence. I'd earlier asked you the question about the HV special police and the military police. On the third line it says: "At the same time a mop-up operation took place." What do you term to be in this sentence "a mop-up operation"?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- today I would translate that into an operation looking for pockets of military resistance, operations that would be looking for civilians hiding in shelters, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You observed this from the top of the UN barracks throughout the city of Knin, that a mop-up operation was going on?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were informed by -- by people who were collected and dropped at the gate of the barracks that this was in fact going on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So that's not something that you saw. That's something that you heard from someone who came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I think you told us before that at least regarding the special police, you had not observed them engaging in any kind of mop-up operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever observe a mop-up operation firsthand, anywhere?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have no recollection of anything that is not reported at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, you don't know it is done or who does it or what -- or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now your military experience, Mr. Hansen, was as an officer in the Danish army in the armoured infantry; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an is reserve officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long ago was that? Are you still a reserve officer today?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't served since 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So 1991 was the last time you were a reserve officer or the last time you were a full-time officer?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been a full-time officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, P1284 is your 1997 statement, Mr. Hansen. And the first page of the statement, other than the cover page, the first paragraph the first full paragraph where it says: "I am here to make a statement," the second line toward the end of that line of that particular paragraph says: "I understand that should the individuals I can give evidence against be charged as war criminals." Who were the individuals you could give evidence against? Did you have someone in mind at the time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Further on in this particular statement where it says: "The standard procedure." "The standard procedure was that following patrols or meetings, daily reports were written, and in my capacity as team leader, I was the author of all these reports." Now, there were days when daily reports were not written. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the reason that daily reports were not written on certain days?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If no activity took place on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, toward the end of August of 1995, at least from the documents that we see that are being tendered through you, there were several days that did not have reports. You were not there during that time-period when some of these reports were written; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. I'm leaving the place around the 17th, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you not return until sometime September 2nd, I believe?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if not later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now was there any disciplinary measure taken as a result of somebody not writing a report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is fair to say that if activities could also include administrative issues that were not reported, reorganisation, and certainly also if you're looking for accommodation or office space, that is not an operational activity that would be reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now in these reports if something was reported to you -- strike that question. When you were putting together your reports, can you describe for what you say your methodology was. Did you gather reports from several people and put them into one report? Can you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who undertook meetings or patrols would do their own reports. And then they will be submitted to the next level in the chain of command, and they will be compiled into a summary report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then where would your report go?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on what I'm doing at the time of writing. If I'm the team leader, I would send my reports to the Coordination Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Which was where?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, I think it is in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then from there would it go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would go to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now you would -- in P1285, which is your statement of 2008, you further describe in paragraph 7 that: "Each patrol team had a deadline to send its daily report before a certain time in the evening." And that "it was common procedure that everyone in the team agreed to the contents of the reports before sending it." Now, were you one that went out in the field, or were you one who stayed primarily back compiling the reports?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our August activities, I was also in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now what -- your field work would be you would decide to go in a certain area, you would do a patrol, and you would come back and write a report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 8 of this particular statement, which is the next page on the screen, you return from leave on September 5th, after leaving on the 17th of August. Who was the person who took your place while you were gone?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A fellow countryman called -- by the name Soren Liborius.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you then worked in Zagreb from the 23rd of September; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You worked in Zagreb from September 23rd.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your function there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was operational officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Which meant?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I would be -- find myself in the receiving end of daily reports from teams in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what you do with those reports? Would you summarize them --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would summarize them and forward them through the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now paragraph 16, you state in the last sentence of paragraph 16: "Since nothing was done to control the situation, we had to assume it was all part of a higher plan, or at least an implicit acceptance of it." Now, other than making that conclusion, did you ever speak with anyone that told you that there was a plan or there was an implicit acceptance of looting and burning and harassment?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this -- today, I don't remember having any discussion with anyone about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, it was in fact quite the opposite. You were being told by people that things were trying to be investigated, that looting and burning were trying to be stopped; correct? I mean, they didn't say, Yes, we're going to continue to loot and burn; right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I only refer to my own observations during patrols and in August and early September that it did take place at a large-scale. And irrespective of our meetings with General Gotovina or General Cermak, it -- during which we informed about what we saw, it still continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, did you not get any information or seek any information regarding people that were charged, people that were prosecuted or people that were convicted of committing these acts, did you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you don't know who or if anyone was charged, prosecuted, or convicted or the numbers of those people. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now if we go through P1300 which is a report of the 4th through the 6th of August, which is a daily monitoring activity report, in this report -- were you the author of this report, by the way?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. This report is released by the ECMM headquarters in Zagreb, and I was, at this time, in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So do you recognise anything in this report that you may have contributed, as someone in Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You do, or you do not? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. What section?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Section 3, ECMM in Knin reports on 5th August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where you say: "On 5 August the HV made significant gains."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would that be on page ...

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my screen I have the first page of the report, the summary section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we -- is there something on the summary section that you recognise that you had written?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not my wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't we go to the next page. I'm just interested, Mr. Hansen, in the parts that you recall that you might have written.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, whatever is stated in this report is a summary and extract of -- of team reports coming in. And now, more than 13 years after, I do not recall if a particular sentence is a copy of my own wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not asking for that degree of specificity. I'm just wondering if there is it an area of this report that you recognise that you may have contributed to, and if you can't, that's fine. That is perfectly understandable. Where did you get the information on, for example, on the second page where it says: "The HV made significant gains in a number of key areas"? Where did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is it not my report, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why don't we go to P1290. This is your report, P1290, the comprehensive survey report; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On this cover page, where did you get this cover page from, this map?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think from a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So this wasn't a map that you received either from the UN military observers or --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, maybe the UN Military Observer, yeah. That may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you just can't remember where you got it from?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go to page 1 of your report, the first full page, which in the last four digits on the bottom are 1801.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the page after this, Madam Registrar. If we go to the lower third of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's a paragraph that starts: "Towards the end of July." And there's a notation there where it says: "1 August, Croatian radio and television reported that Gospic was shelled by Serbs. Due to restriction of movement, United Nations Military Observers were unable to conduct crater analysis." Whose restriction of movement are you referring to? Is that the Serbs restricting the movement to get to Gospic from Serb-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now Gospic was a Croatian town; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it would have been shelled from Serb-occupied Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the subject of the UNMO's investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now the Croatians certainly wouldn't forbid them to come in to observe damage from Serb shelling, would they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Go to the next page, please. The second paragraph starts with: "At 0500 hours." In the second sentence it says: "HV engaged ARSK positions all along the ZOS," and I presume that is Zone of Separation; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "However, during the first day, no major breakthrough was accomplished." Now where did you get the information that during the first day no major breakthrough was accomplished? Were you aware of the break through that happened in the Velebit mountains on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you weren't aware that the key location of Mali Alan was taken in the Velebit mountains on the first day?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Later in the same paragraph it says: "Shortly after the meeting it was advised by Radio Knin that the civilian population in the Krajina should evacuate." Did you hear this radio broadcast?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not personally. I would assume I got it from -- this piece of information from my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter that worked me -- worked with me since I came in -- in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So this is an interpreter supplied by the RSK for you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. She was employed by the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: A person of Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This first particular paragraph, full paragraph discusses nothing about operations in the northern part of Sector South. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page -- the last four digits are 1806. And the bottom paragraph. There's a section in this particular part of your report that deals with the Plavno valley. Now, the second sentence says: "A visit to the site revealed that the entire hamlet of Grubori numbering 20 houses was ablaze." Where did you get information about the number of houses?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was our own counting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the ECMM there on the 25th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it looked -- certainly this report somehow indicates that we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now do you know who was there from the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Because, personally, I was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll get to that in a second. It says further in the paragraph: "Three panic stricken elderly women were at the location. The rest of the villagers had gone down the hill for a meeting with UN personnel and had reportedly also been urged to leave by Croatian military uniformed personnel." Now, there is no indication in this particular -- for the source of this particular information; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Later in that paragraph at the bottom it says: "The same evening," meaning the same day, August 25th, 1995, "the HRAT returned to the site," and we'll go to the next page, "and found the bodies of two murdered individuals among the ruins." And there's a description of the victims. The second is described as having his throat deeply slashed with a knife. Where were -- what was the source of information for you here?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I don't recall today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P2158, please. And the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P2158, Mr. Hansen, is an ECMM daily monitoring report of 29 August. And the second page of this document under section 2, political situation, second paragraph presents, again, a description similar but not the same --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to the one in your report. This section states: "A Human Rights Action Team found the bodies of five persons who had been recently killed in the village of Grubori. "On 25 August one 70-year-old man was found dead with a gunshot wound at the back of his skull, and another 65-year-old man had his throat slit."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, that is opposite from what is described in your report.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But, again, I mean, this is it not in any way personal observations, and -- and so I have -- I have no additional comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph it says: "ECMM was informed about seven old women from the Plavno area whose houses had been burnt down in the last few days, two of them witnessed the murder of their husbands. One was burnt alive in his house and the other had his throat slit." Now, this particular report now says that two people witnessed the murder occur, not that two murder victims were found.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But again, sir, I was not even in the country at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, but this is a document that's being tendered through you, Mr. Hansen. And you can't enlighten us any further; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. It is a report from the ECMM headquarters in Zagreb, and I was in Denmark at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go to 65 ter 7018.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. The previous document, P2157 had been MFIed as a bar table submission, not that Mr. Kuzmanovic has discussed with the witness. I don't know if we can enter it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have a problem with that, Your Honour. It is actually P2158, if I'm not mistaken. 65 ter 3532, which is MFI P2158, I will tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you tender that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a bar table submission document, Your Honour. We didn't have any objection to it, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now I understand. You do not object to the document to be admitted, the document which was tendered by Mr. Hedaraly. Yes, now I understand. I was a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then at least P2158 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And just to finish off this theme, Mr. Hansen, 65 ter 7018 is an August 28th daily report from the ECMM. If we look at the bottom of the page, it says: "On returning to UN SS," if we could enlarge that, please. It's the last -- basically, there's a dash before the word "on," which may indicate a paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could have that enlarged, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It says: "On returning to UN SS," and then there's a redaction, presuming that is a person, "was informed of seven old women from the Plavno region who had just been brought into the camp by UNCIVPOL. The women's houses had been burned down in the last few days and two had witnessed the murder of their husbands. One was burnt alive in his house; the other had his throat slit." So that's a third version of the incident that's described in your report, P1290 at pages 6 and 7; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, we had a pathologist testify by the name of Dr. Clark, and the references for his testimony for the Court's benefit, are pages 14278 through 14280. And Dr. Clark, when conducting his analysis of this death, found that there was no one that had a deeply slashed throat, that this comment in these reports that had been spread throughout from report to report, was not accurate. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you also aware that one of these individuals was found by Dr. Clark to have been -- died of gunshot wounds, six of them?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I was not even in the country at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go back to -- I'd like to tender 7018, Your Honour, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit D1273.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1273 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go back to P2158, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One section on this document, Your Honour, and then it's a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P2158, Madam Registrar, please. If we could go to the second page of that document. And if we could scroll down a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, this is a document that I had spoken to you about earlier, the second of the three descriptions of this event in Grubori, all of which have differences. If you look up at the top, where it says "above the political situation section."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's a paragraph that says: "Former Sectors North and South: Serb soldiers continue to surrender in former Sector South. Nine of them did so to the HV in the Podinarje valley which is seven kilometres east of Knin under UN observation. ECMM and the UN are trying to monitor their surrender. Coordination between international organisations and Croatian anti-terrorist groups is expected to be established soon." Now the incident in Grubori which was described below and the surrender of soldiers east of Knin was going on roughly at the same time; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware there were pockets of Serb soldiers in areas that were surrendering or being forced to surrender after Operation Storm had been concluded?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I will have to -- to go back to the time. And commenting on it, I can say that I don't have any proof of evidence that they were there, but I would suspect -- suspect that -- that pockets of resistance of soldiers were left behind in a very chaotic situation so -- and therefore also justifying the mop-up operation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So this particular document, it discusses the surrender is an ECMM document; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an ECMM headquarter report we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. However, before we take a break I would already invite Madam Usher to take Mr. Hansen out of the courtroom because we have to deal with one procedural issue not in any way related, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, I'd like to go back to your report, P1290. And the page at the top is page 12, but the number at the low -- bottom right is 1812. The bottom paragraph. Mr. Hansen, this report that you wrote in September of 1995 on this particular section, bottom paragraph states: "The wish to use the burnings as a psychological operation designed to raise fear among the remaining Serb population in Sector East and in the western part of Bosnia and Herzegovina. From a military point of view, this is a good opportunity to use well known standard techniques: The aim of this psy-ops is to facilitate the expected fighting for the desired terrain. By creating an impression with the enemy that the war is merciless, that no prisoners or property will be spared. The enemy, in this case, is likely to flee in large numbers." And before we get to the reasoning behind this paragraph, you do realize, Mr. Hansen, that when you refer to Sector East, that part of Croatia was peacefully re-integrated back into Croatia, was it not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall Sector East, Vukovar, that part of Croatia, boarding on the Danube with Serbia was peacefully reintegrated back into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, right. Okay, sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you told us before that you were reserve military officer having completed your service in 1991. Can you tell me, please, what military or intelligence training has allowed you to make this type of conclusion that you did on bottom of page 12?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had certainly -- I was -- trained on a number of occasions in intelligence, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You're not seriously telling us that burnings were used as a psychological operation to raise fear among the remaining Serb population in Sector East, are you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have no further comment to the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go to the same report, page 18; the last four digits on the bottom of the document are 1818. Before I get to that question, let me ask you one more question about that statement that you made about psychological operation. You have no documentation or you have you not talked to anyone within the Croatian military or any military that has led to you come to any evidence to base that conclusion upon; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back to this particular reference on page 18 at the very bottom it says: "The people had been mobilized in Serbia and brought to Krajina, and, as it is known, it was a great hunt after them." Now was this information that people were mobilized in Serbia and brought to Krajina received from your one of your contacts, Serb contacts within the former Krajina?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, today, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know whether people were mobilised in Serbia and brought to occupied parts of Croatia to fight?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot verify this information today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go -- there's a term you had used, administrative cleansing. Maybe not necessarily in this report. But I know I have seen it in ECMM documents. You know what I'm referring to, are you not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. As a matter of fact, there is there was a Hungarian diplomat that came and was part of a tour that you gave; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Than was his term, administrative cleansing; correct? Or self-ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall if he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you mean administrative cleansing, did you meaning something to the effect that the Serbs themselves administratively left. Is that what you mean by administrative ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall today the administrative cleansing would refer to the complication associated with the claim of property and with the application of citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: After people had left?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now you realize that few, if any, of those people had any personal identification documents?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we go to P934, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, before we leave your report, 1290, you had an annex to that document, Annex 3, and I wanted to ask you some questions about that. We don't necessarily have to put it up. But Annex 3 was the list that you were provided of damage, of property damage to villages and towns in Sector South; correct? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now as with the reporting on various ECMM reports on Grubori, there are other incidents specifically in your comprehensive survey where you to rely on other reports; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, an example in Annex 2 is you reliance on the UNMO survey of damages; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That was something that the UNMOs gave you to, and you simply included it in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now you do not know what the methodology was used that they employed or how they categorised homes, for example, based on damage; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know how they accounted for Croatian villages versus Serbian villages; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it's fair to say that you cannot attest to the accuracy of that particular survey; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- the reason it is included is not because of any reference to accuracy but more an indication of the level of destruction. So the accuracy of the numbers are not the most important in -- in this attachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, would you agree with me that if there was, for example, a village that had listed 20 buildings in it before Operation Storm and 18 of those buildings were listed as partially damages and then 20 were listed as totally damaged, that is it not accurate.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P934, the second page, please. Under Section C. And just for reference, this is an August 11th, 1995, ECMM report. You were not in Sector South on the 11th of August; correct.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, you were there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I thought you had said had you left on the --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 17th. I'm sorry, you are correct. Section C under team Knin, it describes 70 soldiers in Gracac and around the same number who said they were from the 150th brigade in Medak. Now were you aware at any point time that as of the date of this report, 11th of August, 1995, that anyone -- that any special police forces were located in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And this report is from N3, and I was not a member of that team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So the fair answer to that question is you don't know.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, section G.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's another team Knin N2. Were you part of N2?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a part of that team, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There's a comment here that says: "The Catholic church in Vrlika recently destroyed with Serb graffiti on the walls." There is no indication of when that was put on the walls; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yet in the common section it says: "Team had interviewed Serb refugees in the camp who were from that area, and they said that the church was untouched when they left after the shelling had started. They believed that the damage may have been done by the HV in order to put the blame on the Serbs." And then the comment says: "This seems fairly sensible as it is unlikely that people fleeing for their lives would stop to write nasty messages on a wall." Now how could you come to the conclusion that a recently destroyed church Serb graffiti on the walls was plausibly destroyed by the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today I have no further comment. I mean, the general picture when it comes to churches is that they were left standing and untouched and bypassed throughout the operation, and this a single event, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that in the middle of Knin, St. Anthony's church was significantly damaged?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So -- and that's a catholic church; right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a catholic church. But not during my presence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were aware that during -- before operation storm that it was routine practice for the Serbian ARSK forces to destroy Catholic churches?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw destruction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And yet in this particular passage, you find plausible that the Croatian military destroyed their own Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't find that plausible?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In the next section under section 4, discussing team Gospic in a field full of cattle. There is a statement: "There is evidence of the systematic rounding up and shipment of livestock from all over the former Krajina. Their destination is unknown, but it is unlikely they are being saved for reclamation by the Serb population which are officially being urged to return." How do you know that it was the Croatian government -- strike that. Now, what other method did the Croatian government have that you could tell us to reserve livestock that had been abandoned in the flight of the Serb population? If there is no Serb population to take care of the livestock, are they just supposed to stay there in the fields?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, I think it was -- I thought, and I still think, that it was a sensible thing to collect the cattle in order to save guard it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So rather than being something that was nefarious or something that was done to discourage the Serbs from returning, it was something done to save the cattle?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, if the cattle is left without any observation, I mean, it's a sensible thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next -- P935. It's a 13th of August ECMM report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, there's discussion here under political assessment. Could you tell me, were an author of this report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have been. It could be. I'm not totally sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going ask you who else might have been. I just want to know --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could easily have been one of the authors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. The first paragraph describes the mayor of Knin: "A Serbian man who has no history, as far as we can tell, of any kind in politics. He is expected to be a puppet for the controlling Croatian authorities and purely a figurehead for the world to see how 'well' the remaining Serbs are being treated by Croats?" What is the basis for that statement?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can certainly say it is not my wording and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the feeling that this man was a puppet?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we are talking about who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The mayor of Knin. That's --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And who is that at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's not listed in this particular --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure there was a mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the government representative of Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Because as far as I remember, there is no mayor at this particular point in time. That would have been General Cermak. No, he arrived evening later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Below it is listed as Petar Pasic at the bottom of this particular document, if we could scroll up.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had no reason to believe that he was a puppet, was he?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To this very day, I mean, I don't -- I cannot comment on that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now at the bottom of this particular document, there's also a request for assistance of ECMM in persuading the remaining ARSK troops hiding in the hills around Medak to give themselves up. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At least there's another comment here as of the 13th August of 1995 that someone, specifically Mr. Kasumovic has reported that there are ARSK troops hiding in the hills; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if question go to 2 on the next page, military assessment. The middle of that paragraph, the first paragraph under military assessment. Actually, we can go a little farther up than that. Fifth line at the very end of that line, the sentence begins: "It is ..." "It is assessed that the swiftness of the success of Operation Storm caught not only the HV by surprise but also the civilian authorities who were supposed to go in afterwards and take over. Consequently as the 'capital' fell in 36 hours instead of the expected week, the military and civilian police who were next to arrive did so late. The civilian authorities were also caught on the hop and have not been able to bring their move forward at all." Now, I'd like to ask you a question of what is meant by "the capital fell in 36 hours instead of the expected week"? Was that an assessment that you made, that you thought it would take a week to get to Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I was absolutely not the author of this paragraph. For me, the importance of -- of -- of this text lie in the fact that -- that Knin was taken within 36 hours. And my assessment is that it appeared to be a surprise to both the HV and the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was it a surprise to the ECMM as well?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a surprise to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now if we go to P2150. And if we go to the second page of P2150. This is an August 9th, 1995, ECMM report. And on the bottom of the second page, under political situation, there is a significant redaction about presumably names or ranks of people, and it states: "Blank met with blank, who stated that the number of Croatian fatalities during Operation Storm was 118, with 40 in the Sisak area. Blank added that the Croatian authorities had anticipated 5 to 6.000 losses by calculating 5 to 6 per cent of the 100.000 HV troops. Furthermore, blank expected the initial numbers to increase due to the 'cleaning' of the mountainous areas." Now that tells me, and let me ask you if it tells you, that the Croatian military, along with the assessment made in the previous exhibit which was P935, certainly did not expect to take Knin in 36 hours and was prepared for losses of up to 6.000 of its troops.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is pretty clear, at least from their own assessment, that they thought this was going to be much more difficult than it ended up being?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. We all thought that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You also thought that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is not unexpected that they wouldn't be ready after taking Knin so quickly?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is -- I think it is a surprise to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to go to the next page of P -- I'm sorry. If we go back to P935. I'm done with P2150. The same page we were on P935 which was the second page. 1079 are the last four digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And, again, for reference, it's Sunday, 13th of August, 1995, ECMM report. Again, another mention under military assessment and analysis at the bottom of the first paragraph about "the presence in the hills of ARSK troops who cause trouble at night." Again, noting that there are pockets of resistance; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go to the next page, which is 1080, under humanitarian assessment. The first sentence -- the first two sentences of that assessment say: "A well-planned and carefully executed clean-up operation has been in action through [sic] the week. The Croatian army and police have swept up through the former RSK, removing evidence." The first thing I'd like to ask you is what are you talking about when you say "a well-planned and carefully executed clean-up operation"? What is that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that. But it is being tendered -- or it was being referenced through you, Mr. Hansen. Can you tell us anything or shed any light on this?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I'll have to translate it, and the way I'll translate such a sentence would be that -- that the HV would be looking for pockets of resistance and control of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what -- what is meant by the term "removing evidence"? Evidence of what?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you say --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The next page, 1081. It says in the middle of that page where the paragraph says: "Rural areas." The second sentence says: "Knin town and immediate surroundings have suffered only superficial damage." What is that based on, a review of the damage situation in the town?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, from a personal point of view, in the assessment on the damage in Knin town itself, would be initiated by my own fact finding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it was that it was superficial?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the correct term would be that it is not structural.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The report says superficial, though. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Again, I did not write this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of what the civilian casualties were in Knin as a result of the shelling on the first two days of --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P895, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going preface my question relating to P985 by a comment that you had made, I think it was both in direct examination and in the answers to questions from my colleague, Mr. Cayley. You had said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you misspoke and that we're still talking about 895, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I said 985 it is a mistake. It is 895.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 895. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is my temporary dyslexia. 895. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had mentioned that when you saw presumably displaced persons, Croatian displaced persons come back, that they came back as tourists. Describe for me what you meant by that. Were they coming back to see the state and shape of their residences?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in order for me to say that, I would have to make a direct connection between a person and -- and his ownership of a certain property, and I was not able to do that. But in general terms we saw many, many civilians or -- and Croats coming back to -- well, to see the situation for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not just Croats but persons of Serb ethnicity as well?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean there is no distinction. From a distance, a Serb and a Croat look alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My question relating to this issue is -- in this report under political situation, 20th September, 1995, where it describes the revitalisation of Lovinac, 50 to 60 native-born persons are already in the village trying to repair their former homes. Now, did you -- were you under the -- did you know that that town had been levelled after 1991, Lovinac?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, perhaps at the time I was aware of it. Today, I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, these people who would be coming back, according to this report, repairing their former homes would not be tourists; correct? And as a matter of fact, in annex of damages to villages, Lovinac is not a place that is not included; did you know that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There is also mention here, There is a police station manned by special police. Now can you tell me anything specific about what that means?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P1288, please. This is a September 12th, 1995, ECMM daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the question I want to ask you relates to a military situation where you state in the second line -- or where it is stated in the second line: "Suspected cleaning operation, ongoing in the north of the sector around Seganovac by special police." Were you there to observe that at all?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what they mean "suspected cleaning operation"?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you know why someone say it was suspected?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would be sheer speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P936, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a report listed with you listed as the author, Mr. Hansen, dated August 16th of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Under Benkovac it's listed: "We passed three check-points on the entrance roads to the town, which has a seemingly [sic] little damage?" Now did you know that Benkovac was one of the towns that was attacked with artillery on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And there is no indication of Benkovac being torched or looted, is there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just like the other urban centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Under the next section where it says Tomasovica Stanovi, it says: "This small village was not damaged but deserted except two old people who were very hungry. They don't know where the other people are, even their children are gone. They have no place to go and are anxious to be killed." Now, that is clearly a mistake, is it not? Those people weren't anxious to be killed, were they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is simply just a missing syntax; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Further on down under humanitarian and human rights issue, toward the middle of the page, it says: "The extensive cleaning operation after Storm makes it hard to witness HRV." Now, this is a document in which you at author, and you use the term "cleaning operation." Can you tell us, please, what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, again, it is variations over the same theme, and it's about the HV looking for pockets of resistance, cleaning up the area, controlling the area, and -- which you would expect any army in the offensive to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, there is no indication here that they're hiding, doing anything incorrect or wrong; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you note here "many teams fear the mine risk, and so far only main roads have been patrolled by HRAT." Now, mines were a significant hazard to movement, correct, especially in areas that were off the main roads?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what is revealed in this text is that there is no hard evidence of presence of mines, but the speculation into the presence of mines prevented people going to particular sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were aware that after Cambodia and Bosnia, Croatia was the most mined country in the world?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was certainly aware of it in other places, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P1287, please. Your Honour, this subject area is the last subject area I will cover. It is hopefully not too extensive, but I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Hopefully in the next 15 minutes I'll be done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then we will have to take a break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll break, if that's all right with Your Honour. Because this is a new subject that teals with this report, and after I'm done with this report, I'm done with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means just for me to do some -- to give an assessment. So that is 20 more minutes for you, then for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have about two sessions. Under three hours. I tried to cut it down, but about three hours, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 20 minutes. Then, Mr. Hedaraly, how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Up to now, probably only five to ten minutes, but, of course, it is going to depend on the Gotovina cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because I -- in the difficult choice between the lunch freaks and the early weekend freaks, the Chamber thought it wise to give an additional 15 minutes, but Mr. Kehoe, if you're not fully confident to stay strictly within your time limits, it will cut off from your lunchtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll stay within those time-limits, Your Honour. Actually, I'm confident I'll stay within that. I think Mr. Kuzmanovic covered some things that I'm going cut out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you might even need less than three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I never like to see it [indiscernible], Judge, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
