utterances.text: Then we earlier had some confusion about who tendered what document and whether it was page 68, line 1, included Mr. Misetic without any proper reason to add to the confusion. That is clearly a mistake. The document was tendered by Mr. Hedaraly. Then the Chamber would need -- one more question: How time did you need to give a respond to the five questions? The first question being answered already by kind of a schedule for the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have elected Mr. Cayley to speak for us all on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, could you speak for you all, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have actually just this moment sent an e-mail to the Prosecution and your Senior Legal Officer. So we can also make oral submissions in addition, but we've answered the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a long lunch break anyhow, so we can look at it. Then we take a break now, Mr. Hansen, and we'll resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.44 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, I found the reference regarding the term self-ethnic cleansing in P1289 which is September 12th, 1995, report that you had offered, ECMM report. And it was regarding the Hungarian ambassador, Mr. Cermati. And he asked questions, Why did the Serbs flee in front of the CA, Croatian army? And then it's noted after the question, he, meaning the ambassador, called it "self ethnic cleansing." Do you know what he meant by that term that you put in your report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask Mr. Registrar to please call up 65 ter 7007.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This particular document, 65 ter 7007, is a weekly assessment, 31 July to 3 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page -- on the right-hand side, it's R026-4155. It's the third page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Under humanitarian situation, at this particular time between the 31st of July and the 3rd of August 1995, you were in Knin, correct, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In this notation under humanitarian situation, there's a total of 18.000 displaced persons and refugees in Sisak Zupanija and 16.000 in Karlovac Zupanija, and 15.000 in the town of Ogulin, for a total of 37.500 displaced persons. Those are all Croatian displaced persons; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Sisak Zupanija, Karlovac Zupanija, and Ogulin were Croatian towns?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. But these locations are totally out of -- outside the area of my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that: "RC Knin reported that RSK would not hinder the UNHCR delivery of humanitarian aid to the Bihac pocket within the same section under humanitarian situation." Is it your understanding that you -- you can't tell us whether these displaced persons are Croats?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I can certainly say that it makes a lot of sense if they are, but, again, I mean, I'm -- it's information that has to do with the area that is total outside my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Back on that subject of self-ethnic cleansing, if we could go to P --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. If we could tender 65 ter 7007. I forgot to do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is document shall be given Exhibit D1274. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1274 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On page 14 of P1290, if I could ask Mr. Registrar to please call that up, the last four numbers on the bottom right-hand corner of the page are 1814.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting to get to that -- oh, there it is. Mr. Hansen, in your own report there's a section called "self-ethnic cleansing" which was referred to by the Hungarian ambassador; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And in this section, it states: "On several occasions it has been discussed why the Krajina Serb population ran away in front of the advancing HV troops. The term self-ethnic cleansing has been used and indicates that the Serb population left due to RSK indoctrination through the last four years. The term gives responsibility for the exodus to the Serbs themselves and release anybody else." Now the issue of self-ethnic cleansing is something that you, yourself, put in your report and is something that you heard from someone who was not a party to the conflict, meaning the Hungarian ambassador; correct.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please pull up P1287. And while it's coming up, I'll advise everyone that it is a September 9th, 1995, ECMM report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The second page of this document, Mr. Hansen, in the second full paragraph, includes a fairly extensive discussion about an interview given by the vice-president of the Sabor, Vladimir Seks. Do you understand that the Sabor is the Croatian parliament?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In that interview he is described as being utterly uncompromising in his standpoint over property rights of the Croatian Serbs stating that "there are no rules here." Seks said that "private property of the Serbs who have left Croatia must be part of the final division of liabilities and claims."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like Mr. Registrar to please call up 3D01-0827 via Sanction, please. It's not necessary to do it via Sanction. It has been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And while it is coming up, Mr. Hansen, we were able to obtain a copy of this interview that was used as a reference source for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And on this particular topic, if we could go to page 5 of the English version and page 3 of the B/C/S. If we could scroll down to the very bottom, where it starts with: "That's the legal situation." And I'll just represent to you that this document, the bold are the questions or the comments from the author of the interview, or the questioner, and the remaining portion which is not in bold are the responses in this text. It's a September 4th, 1995 interview. And the question is, preface to this, is why there was a state of war proclaimed between Croatia and Serbia relating to war operations. And the question is: "That's the legal situation. However, what are the actual chances to get war reparations from Serbia?" Seks answers: "Factually there are no records in history that somebody paid war reparations if they did not capitulate at whole if it wasn't occupied, and if paying war reparations were not imposed to it. "Question: So it is like, 'Who cares. No harm done.' "Answer: Croatia has already seized all property that was in social ownership by Serbia and Montenegro. "Question: The same as they have seized all of Croatian property. How does the law regulate private ownership? "Answer: Since what happened is a country falling apart and creation of new ones, several solutions are possible in order to compensate war reparations to Croats." If we could go to the next page, I'm sorry, in English. Thank you. Thank you to my colleague for noticing that. I left off Your Honours in the second line of that second -- the next page. "Several solutions are possible in order to compensate war reparations to Croats. A, a complete war defeat, total capitulation, and imposed payments. That's not realistic to happen. B, after the war has completely ended and the relations have been normalised, to solve the question of war reparations by arrangement. This is as realistic to happen as A. C, to bring a suit against Serbia before the Tribunal in The Hague which is depends on the principle of voluntariness; therefore, that's unrealistic as well. D, you can say it this way: We have finally got rid of everything, and that's the lowest price we could have paid. E, regarding the breakup of Yugoslavia and everything said from A to D, ... I personally think the same, a law on succession should be applied on private ownership of the ones who left Croatia of their own accord. "Question: Can you be a by the more specific? "Answer: Specifically that means that the private ownership of Serbs who left Croatia should enter a phase of final division of obligation and demand in probate proceedings called succession in former Yugoslavia. That's in case, if war reparations, are not compensated nor charged. "Question: Does that mean that Croatia would take such goods and turn them into succession estate and leave to Serbia to settle the debts to their citizens? "Answer: That's right. "Question: Does that apply on summer houses owned by Serbs in Croatia? "Answer: Yes, it does." If we could go to the next page in English. "Question: Would such proceedings be in accordance with international regulations? "Answer: There are no rules. It is a matter of conventions an actual relations. Never in history had a country fallen apart under the same circumstances as Yugoslavia had."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go back to the statement that was made in this report, Mr. Hansen, P1287.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I'm going too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was not an invitation to stop completely, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, based on the original text of the interview and on the excerpt here that is taken out of the interview in this report, you would agree with me, would you not, that the statement that the standpoint over property rights of Croatian Serbs stating there are no rules here does not mean that in any way, shape, or form, the interview stated that Croatian Serbs would have their property confiscated or uncompensated; correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to say that that ECMM report that you refer to is a weekly assessment issued by the ECMM headquarters. An assessment at this point is a report that would reflect over actual reports, daily reports, from the preceding week, and, as such, I have no stake at all in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Hansen. My question to you is, since this report has been tendered through you, as a witness, would you agree with me, based on your reading of what was quoted in the ECMM report and what Mr. Seks actually said is taken completely out of context?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The mere fact that the document was tendered through Mr. Hansen does not mean that he can necessarily provide factual information about it. So in that respect I would object to Mr. Kuzmanovic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think as a matter of fact, that Mr. Kuzmanovic is seeking any factual information. He is just seeking from this witness an opinion, an opinion about whether what is in the ECMM report is supported by the text of the interview itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is, by the way, a question which, of course, could be answered by the Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: True, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you want to -- although it's a witness of fact who has clearly stated several times that sometimes that he did not observe matters himself or that he wasn't the author of the report, and since we had heard Mr. Hedaraly does not object against seeking an opinion of this witness, I won't stop you, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, you've heard me and you've read the version that I have read to you and you have seen what was in the ECMM memory report. You would agree with me, would you not, from your reading of both what I read to you and what you have read in the ECMM report that Mr. Seks' statement is taken completely out of context?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a discrepancy between the two texts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the earlier paragraph, in 1289, if could I please go back to -- I'm sorry, 1287.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I'm going to be flipping back and forth between 1287 and this 3D document, just so you know. If we could go back to that same page R026-5902 of P1287.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the top of this page where the paragraph begins: "Statements ..." And I'll read to that you, Mr. Hansen: "Statements from high-ranking Croatian politicians of late have demonstrated that in the aftermath of Operation Storm, there appear to be no indications of moderation of Croatian politics. In fact, on the contrary, the Hawks within the Sabor seem to be taking advantage of the current international attention in order to promote the image that Croatia, as the injured party, is merely attempting to redress the balance. President Tudjman's claim of 'an eye for an eye' as justification of the appalling destruction of Serb property in the former Sectors North and South being just one example of this." I'd like to go back to the 3D document, 3D01-0827. In this particular first page of this interview, the preface of the interview, the second paragraph talks about the inventories of Hawkism and describes in the third line Mr. Seks as a hawk. And nowhere in this particular document or in this particular interview is there anywhere a quote from President Tudjman claiming "a eye for an eye" as any kind of a justification. Now, can you tell me, Mr. Hansen, where the source of this claim that President Tudjman justified anything as a eye for an eye?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. And, again, it's not my report, it's not my wording. I have no reference to this at all. [Indiscernible] by the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I urged Mr. Kehoe to stay within his time-limits. You are now almost 20 minutes. You are you over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have one further question or set of questions relating to part of the interview, and I'm done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please try to wrap up as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Staying with this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as long as have it, I might as well tender it right now. I'm still going to be using it, but I will tender it for the moment, since I'm going to be going back and forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections from the Prosecution, Mr. Hedaraly. Then, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given exhibit number D1275. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the English, and we can stay with page 1 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The question at the top of the page relates to a discussion regarding, at the time Serbian President Milosevic. "Question: Does that mean that the Serbian president was left only with Bosnia as the only territory to manipulate and to expand to. "Answer: Exclusively. Milosevic is in a pretty unenviable situation. He is in a situation to mark Karadzic's option as hazardous in case that the Bosnian leader does not accept the plan of the contact group. On the other side, keeping Karadzic's Serbian republic alive is the only way to evade Milosevic's complete defeat. He must force Karadzic to accept the plan of the contact group, because he ensures a territorial entirety that would be connected to Serbia. A modified American plan is completed in a way. "Question: If that was completed, what would be the consequences for Croatia? "Answer: The consequences would be that the stability and safety would be ensured of the most of the national area of Croats in Bosnia and the area that are shared with the Muslims. Safety of those areas and nations would be guaranteed, especially because the Federation has to rely on Croatia for confederate relations. By accepting the American plan, Croatia does not share a direct border with Serbia and can strategically protect the longest and the most vulnerable border." Now, Mr. Hansen, if we could go back to P1287.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The same page we were on before, Mr. Registrar. Second page, please. If we can go down about two thirds -- a little more than halfway down where it says: "Confederal links between the confederation and Croatia." The sentence starts: "Seks said ..." There we go, yes, thank you. If we could highlight that paragraph, please, bottom half of that paragraph. Now, in this particular portion of the ECMM report, taken out of the article, the report says: "Seks said that the Federation 'must entirely rely on confederate relations and links (to Croatia).' And the consequences for Croatia were 'the stability and security of the Croats in Bosnia and the territories which the Croats shared with Muslims.' These comments clearly demonstrate Croatia's goal of a hinder land in Bosnia acting as a buffer zone and the realisation of a 'greater Croatia.'" Now, Mr. Hansen, you would agree with me based on this report and in comparison to the actual interview, there's absolutely nothing in Mr. Seks's answer that says anything about a greater Croatia; correct.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the extra time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hansen, by the way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hansen.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a pleasure to meet you, sir. I will do my best to move through this as quickly as possible so you can get on your way.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'd just like to touch on a couple of things. First, the issue of the evacuation on the 4th that you referred to on page 2 of your diary. Mr. Hansen, prior to the -- prior to Operation Storm, were you aware of plans by the RSK for evacuations?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You mean nobody had told you that they were practicing evacuations or that teams had been set up to make sure that there was fuel and transportation for evacuations?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were aware, however, that people actually wanted to leave the area, let's just say in late July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. And -- and families of people who were working with us left in -- in the late July days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you see quite a few people leave in the late July days, sir?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was aware of the immediate relatives to -- to staff working with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now on the 4th of August, and if we can go to P592, and I'm talking about the afternoon of the 4th of August. We're just going to talk a little bit about this evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't want to interject too quickly. I'm going to let counsel ask questions, but I'm just starting to get a bit concerned because the witness just stated that he knew absolutely about the evacuation on the 4th, so I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, may finish what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, having received the list of documents that Mr. Kehoe intends to use, many of the exhibits relate to evacuation the video, the plans are there, so I just am wondering if it is going to be an exercise in going through these documents and educating the witness on something he has no knowledge about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, as all counsel is aware, that witnesses are not here to learn new things but to tell us what they know, and that is I think already clearly demonstrated by you, Mr. Hansen, when you knew something, you told us; and when you apparently did not know something, you told that as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I direct your attention to this note which was done by a member of the UN Sector South staff concerning a meeting with the ARSK leadership. And you note in your diary at page 2 that there had been a meeting between a UN and the RSK General, and the discussion was the evacuation. Do you know who this ECMM person is that is listed in the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, no?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the -- a person taking part in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how about this, there is an designation towards the end of that paragraph, that notes the ARSK chief of residence evacuation. Did you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let us turn to D182. This is another note by a Colonel Ratsouk of the meeting at the -- with the ARSK. Excuse me, the RSK authorities. As this comes up, Mr. Hansen, you'll note it says, 8 July 1995, the parties have agreed, but it's actually the 4th of August, 1995, so don't be thrown off by that wrong date. I'm interested in the centre because this thereby plays back into your diary. This -- and generally talks about the meeting with Kosta Novakovic. The middle paragraph notes that the RSK authorities have requested UN assistance in organizing and providing transport for such evacuation. RSK initial calculation shows that UN will need to provide for these refugees transportation around 70.000 litres of fuel, and 450.000 trucks [sic]. Excuse me, 450 trucks. That's a lot of trucks, 450.000. 450 trucks, excuse me. "RSK propose one main road from Knin to Padjene, Otric, Srb, Martin Brod, Bosanski Petrovac, Banja Luka." Now, sir, you in your diary learned about this meeting, and you also learned at that meeting that the plan was to go to Bosnia; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. He said that he learned at the meeting. I think he testified that he wasn't at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I also heard you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I misspoke, I may have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You learned about this meeting, and you learned that the RSK was going to evacuate their people to Bosnia, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I was -- I was not taking part in the meeting, and today I -- I don't recall being informed -- or what I was informed about following the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you noted in your diary that you were going to drive with them to Drvar in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was -- sir, that was following the -- the commencement of the operation at a time when -- when civilians were gathering in front of the -- of the main gate to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So at -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Maybe we are talking past each other, and I am referring to the meeting that you talk about in your diary, where you note on page 2 that: "There has just been a meeting between the UN and the RSK General. The aim now is to evacuate the population from the larger towns throughout Sector South."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I -- Your Honour, I think it may be helpful if the witness could look at his diary, that page. It's not up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps for to us look at -- on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, it's tab 21 at P -- it's -- the exhibit is P1292, the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you learned after that meeting that the civilian population was going to be evacuated. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stated here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall this at all?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that we were in some provisionary planning -- were assigned different tasks, and obviously, I was assigned the task of jumping on one of the -- on a vehicle in a convoy. And this planning, by the way, never materialised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that as part of the planning, the evacuation convoy was going to go to Bosnia, that that was the plan?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an entry here, I cannot -- I have no further comment to the entry in the diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does the answer reflect that it was going to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, apart from what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also referred, and I'm not sure, frankly, if it was on your direct this morning or cross-examination with one of my colleagues, but you do refer to it your comprehensive survey - and let me get that - which is P1290 at page 5, page 2 of the actual document, that: "In the evening the sector commander was called for a meeting with ARSK in Knin. He asked to assist in evacuating the population by supplying fuel and transportation."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Shortly after the meeting it was advised by radio that the civilian population in the Krajina should evacuate."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just moving ahead to that same document, and we're talking about -- should be page 16 or 19 as it is uploaded but 16 on the page number top. Your interpreter told you that she was informed by her boyfriend that there was going to be an and I quote your words "an organised evacuation."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah. Does that accurately assess or assist your recollection that there's a meeting, that the evacuation decision is made, and that a radio broadcast when out and that the boyfriend had the idea that it was going be an organised evacuation?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what we're talking about here is a lot of time --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The events here, yeah, have passed -- has passed, and I have absolutely no reason to question my entries and reports or my own diary at this time. We are just talking about 13 years somehow disappeared between the events and our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hansen, I appreciate that, and, please, to the extent that you can help us and answer the questions you can. If you don't recall other than the entries, then just let us know. Okay. I don't want to make this an exercise in too much difficulty for you.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now on a separate note with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On a separate note, independent of the residents that heard the radio report, I just would like to note for you out on page 18 of your comprehensive report, which is, I think, page 21 as it's uploaded but page 18 on the top of the document itself. In the second -- first full paragraph, starting with: "Some of the people ..." If we go down two sentences: "When soldiers found out that they were alone on the front line, without any backup or any support from the high - it should be 'rang' [sic] officers; I suppose it means 'ranking' officers - without communication means, they just decided on their own to pull out."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Then they informed people in the villages close to the positions about withdrawal and whoever wanted to join them were welcome [sic]." So that was based on, I take it, your discussions with people at the time. There was yet another arm of evacuation that the soldiers took people with them that were near the front line.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your quotation is from -- taken from a testimony issued by my interpreters. It is not my text. But what she is informing is that -- there that soldiers were somehow left at the front line and with the command structure disappearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I would like to show you a couple of documents, and it will end in an ECMM report. But just following up on your interpreter, you wrote the report based on what the interpreter told you, believing that she was a dependable source. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just turn to page -- excuse me, P71, 80 in the English, and page 43 in the B/C/S. And this is an operational diary for the Split Military District. So -- an HV operational diary. If we go to page 80 in the English and 43 in the B/C/S, on the right-hand column. And I want to show you at line -- time is 1330 on the 4th: "Enemy lines broken, enemy chaotically running away." 1445: "Seize Badanj and Visibaba, one tank reported." I will tell you that the evidence is that those are features that are up on the Dinara. And just mindful of this time, 1330 to 1445 -- or just 1445, I would like to turn your attention to D137. Now, this is an evacuation order signed by President Martic in Knin on the 4th of August, 1995, at 1645. My first question is did you know that Martic was in Knin on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you aware, were you made aware at any point that he signed an evacuation order at 1645?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware that he signed, but I was aware of a radio broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did ECMM -- let me show you a series of documents. And first it's -- I'm not sure if this is -- this is -- I wanted to go into the level of how ECMM handled this. 65 ter 710, it may very well be a document that counsel has -- it's not -- it's 65 ter 710. It's a weekly assessment for -- 17010 [sic], that's right. I'm sorry, 65 ter 7010. I realize this is a weekly assessment out of Zagreb, sir, so -- but this is for the week 4 to 10, and if we could go to the second page. And they're talking about Operation Storm throughout this, and in the middle of the paragraph, during former Croatian displaced people it notes: "It seems an evacuation order may have been issued." Again, if we could just go into --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could offer this into evidence, Mr. President. 65 ter 7010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections by the Prosecution. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this documents shall be given Exhibit D1276. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1276 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hansen, I am just going to go through a couple of documents with so I can move through this quickly and then I can ask you questions, as opposed to doing it seriatim. The next one is 65 ter 4115 which is a daily monitoring report for 21 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: This one is actually P1297 MFI. It's one of the bar table documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that there is no objection against --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection to the admission, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same for the other Defence teams which means already that P1297 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And going -- this is -- you can see the front sheet of this being a monitoring report for 21 August --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's not the front sheet there. 65 ter 4115. That's it. And if we could go to the last page of this. Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, according to media sources -- and do you see this here, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: According to media sources, the Krajina Serb minister of foreign affairs, Mr. Vojinovic stated on 20 August that the order for the evacuation of civilians from Knin had been issued by Krajina Serb President, Martic. Mr. Vojinovic also said that both Mr. Martic and the Krajina Serb army commander General Mrksic had denied issuing such an order at last week's session of the Krajina -- excuse me, of the Krajina government." And let me just go into one last document, and this would be P798 which is again a ECMM report of mission -- report by head of mission for 15 August 1995. You can take a look at the front sheet, and I'm actually interested in page 3. It's P798 at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I apologise, it's D798. I have written in the outline P and it's actually D. Apologies. And if we could go to the second page at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you need to see the front page again, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you see that -- that -- actually, it's the third page, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Talking about the people leaving: "Their departure seems to be final, but Krajina authorities, and particularly, President Martic encouraged their citizens to leave." Now you were getting quite a bit of information that this was the evacuation that was ordered by the RSK, and they had no intentions of staying in the Krajina once the HV began the attack. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to P889, and this is a sitrep, a weekly sitrep, of the 13th of August, 1995. Just in that summary at the top. In here you call this a -- I trust that you didn't write this, but in this, this is a called at the top a -- "the largest voluntary ethnic cleansing during the entire Balkan conflict." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think you talked about that during your discussions with Mr. Kuzmanovic, and it is likewise in -- I'm not sure. If I may ... P1289, which is a sitrep of the 12th of September, 1995, that discussions the meeting with the Hungarian ambassador Cermati that was talked about before. If we go to -- just note in the one -- first paragraph that Mr. Cermati is meeting with you in Knin, and he goes to the bottom of the page where he notes the that: "Why did the Serbs flee in front of the Croatian army? He called it self-ethnic cleansing." Now this whole idea of self-ethnic cleansing, I mean, you use it, the Hungarian ambassador uses it, there -- as we go through the ECMM reports it's -- has comments that the evacuation was ordered by President Martic. I mean, as you sit here, Mr. Hansen, have you concluded that that evacuation was a voluntarily evacuation that was done at the behest of the leaders of the Republic of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly comes across as an appeal from -- from the president to the population, that an evacuation should take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, Mr. Hansen, you say it certainly comes across. Is that -- are you interpreting the information you now receive and -- or are you referring to what came to your mind at the time, in addition to what we find in the reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I know is that there was a radio broadcast in the afternoon of the 4th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And any additional information is new to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And from what I understand, you say doesn't contradict what my opinion was at the time, based on this information about the radio programme.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to invite to you clearly distinguish between what you remember from the time, what the conclusions were that you made at the time, on the basis of the information you had at that time, and -- because you're not in a position -- of course, you can read or hear what is presented to you, but I would like it know very exactly what is -- what's new to you, and what is, therefore, mainly a matter of conclusions, which may be in line with, and then, of course, we'd like to know, although we might be able even to establish that -- whether something is contradicting. Mr. Kehoe, would you also please try to make this possible for the witness, to always clearly put to him what is the basis for the answers he gives often to composite questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hansen, you were obviously reading these ECMM reports while you were down there, and you in fact gathered more information than just the information you had about the radio report over time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And in monitoring the other information you got from these other sources, you concluded, did you not, that this evacuation was a voluntarily evacuation ordered by the president, Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, from the following day in the morning and then until the 7th, I think, we had no communication means, so, therefore, I did not read any reports. We were then, at that time, relocated to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the weeks that follow when you had the opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Yeah, then we started all reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that that you got a better picture of the actual voluntary nature this evacuation, by reading these reports?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it was not a subject that we were discussing at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's talk about some practical concerns about this evacuation. And you were friends with your interpreter. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personal friends. We had a working relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: A working relationship. I didn't mean anything or than that, sir, please, and pardon me if -- I don't mean that. Just -- just, you know. And you advised her at the time when people were evacuating or people thereafter were leaving and going to Serbia, you advised her to stay. Now, why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my -- my assessment of the situation at that time was that too many civilians had been victim to a political battle, if you like, and I could see that a future as a refugee in Serbia would offer a bleak future, whereas a presence here, where she was born and raised, would offer a prospect for a life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Some years down the line you spoke to her about that decision that she made to stay, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And she thanked you for your advice, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Because she stayed?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She stayed, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And faired and continued to life in the Knin area?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zadar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In Croatia?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Knin is also Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry. That's right. Let me ask you a couple of questions that we talked about, and I'm shifting subjects here, sir. Let me go to some of the items talked about by Mr. Hedaraly. In P2146, which is a sitrep of the 7th of August, it notes that you were speaking to a CALO, and we spoke about permission to go monitoring team N2 area, and he informed us that before clearance from General Gotovina, we are not allowed to accomplish our tasks. Now, this is a time, sir. Was the place where N2 wanted to go, was there troop movements? Was there any type of military activity, given that it was the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point we are confined to the barracks, and what we could see was military movement just outside the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I'm talking about N2. Did N2 want to go to an area where there was military activity, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just wanted to pick up our typical work which was patrolling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But at the time of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the time this was taking place, the 7th of August, there was military activity going on, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know today, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to P860 also it's in tab 6 of your book. Talk about -- it's a sitrep of 10 August 1995. And Mr. Hedaraly addressed this with you. On page 2, it's 3(f). Excuse me, P830. Is that right? P830. Again, this is the 10th of August. "Team Knin report a continuing restriction of movement in trying to get to Benkovac and Obrovac." This is in the second page in paragraph (f) at the top. They were told by the policija -- "on the check-points they can only get to these places with the written permission from General Gotovina." Now at this date on the 10th, again, around Benkovac and Obrovac were there troop movements? Were the HV doing anything militarily there that -- that they wanted to prevent outsiders from coming in and out while they were moving, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. For obvious reasons I'm not able to -- to somehow verify any military activity, but we were for sure prevented from going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand you were not allowed to go there, but you don't know what the HV was doing in the area at that time, do you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: P1288. This is a sitrep for 12 September 1995. Likewise, discuss with Mr. Hedaraly in that first 2(b). "As per order from the Croatian army Ministry of Defence only the Generals Gotovina and Cermak can deal with the international organisation directly." Now when you got that information, you concluded, did you not, that the Ministry of Defence only wanted the higher-ranking people to talk to international organisations so that the Ministry of Defence would speak with one voice. Isn't that what you concluded?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now this is the 12th of September, and I think you noted for us in your -- one of your statements, if I may, this is P1284 at page 4, that the only time you met General Gotovina was this meeting on the 20th of September, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And when you met him -- by the way, did you try to meet him before that or put written requests in to meet General Gotovina before that, that were denied?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you met him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, again. I know my time is somewhat limited. I try to get ahead of myself too much. I apologise. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did know that -- that as of the 6th of August, 1995, that -- that the -- the civilian authorities had taken over in Knin. You did know that, did you not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go through this sitrep just a bit. And this is P895. And you talked about a number of issues. It's coming up right now. A number of issues were discussed. Among them, the possibility of ECMM to patrol at the Bosnian side of the border. "So far it is not possible, and the General promised to inform us." Did you know, Mr. Hansen, that there was ongoing military activity between the HV, HVO, and the ABiH against the Bosnian Serbs and the Krajina Serbs in Bosnia at this time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we know. We knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it was surprise that General Gotovina didn't exactly want you to come up at that particular time to go up to that front line area, was it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had been monitoring wartime events before, so I don't know if it's a surprise or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Asked about -- going back to the report, asked about the ongoing looting, arson, and harassment, "The General's opinion is that police has to control the situation, and Croatia is still a nation with constitution" -- should be law and order. "... any person committing crimes will be charged." Now, in your discussion with him, he never gave you any indication that anybody who committed a criminal act should -- should be -- or they shouldn't be prosecuted, did he?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, he -- he -- he told you that this was a civilian area, and it was up to the police.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Clearly there was a distinction between civilian and military responsibility in his -- in his answer to -- to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, he noted for you, and this the area that -- that was the discussed with Mr. Hedaraly. And it notes that: "However, a war is always followed by disasters, and now things are under control. The General has no objection for Serbs to live in Croatia." But he regards it as "a human feeling to hate an enemy who has burned, looted, and expelled one's families." Now, Mr. Hansen, this was a revenge element that you had recognised in your comprehensive report as something that was pervasive in the area. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And as a man, Mr. Hansen, who lived there and learned what happened and saw what happened, I mean, you could understand what General Gotovina was talking about when he said that people who had been injured had a degree of revenge in their heart?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's just talk about that. Some of the instances that you talk about, and this could very well be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 65 ter 2258. No. 65 ter 2258 is an ECMM report, 7 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not certain who wrote this, sir, so I mean, I know you were there at the time. But if -- this is an ECMM report. And if we can go to the second page of this report.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, it from the humanitarian officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. So you had nothing to do with the report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me just see if you know about it then -- which is -- it's a -- and if we could just look at the -- under the Donji Lepuri, a former Croatian village in RSK, keeping 235 Croatian and 35 Serbian inhabitants. "Humanitarian officer observed several Croatian families repairing their houses. He met the former -- Mr. Juric Branco who told that they are about 30 families rebuilding the farms. They had lived since four years in the homes of their relatives in Zadar and go daily from there to here. Their church is totally [sic] destroyed. The graves were open, and the bones of the buried were thrown around. The houses were looted and burnt in 1991/1992, and the cistern tanks poisoned (dead animals and garbage thrown into). The electricity had been destroyed, and they are waiting now for its reconstruction to be able to stay in the village." Now realising, Mr. Hansen, that this is not yours, it's a humanitarian officer, but this is it pretty much the emblematic of the situation of the returning Serb Croats and what they had gone through. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croat population in the RSK were expelled back in 1991/1992. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And they also suffered quite a bit at the hands of the Serbs before --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During the expulsion, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer 65 ter 2258 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit D1277. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1277 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hansen, you, yourself, talked to people about this, and I want to just chat with you just briefly about one of those incidents, and going back to your diary which is P1290, at tab 21, at page 11 in the hard copy, and it's for the 12th of August of 1995, where you talk about going back to your old headquarters. Do you see that before you, sir? Page --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Page 11.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's D1292 [sic] is the exhibit. P. Excuse me P1292. "We visited our old HQ. It has been visited again, and everything that was removed was destroyed."

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So sorry to interrupt. It's the wrong document on the screen, just for the people that don't have the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm looking at P1292. P1292. Apologies, page 11. At the top of that -- if we go to page 11 of that document. Eleven in the English, in any event. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you with me, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the 12th of August. "We visited our old HQ. It has been visited again, and everything that wasn't removed was destroyed. There was a visit while we were there. A guy in uniform was scouring the building." Now this guy was in what looked like a military uniform, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And he clearly was not operating under orders doing what he was doing at this locale, was he?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "A guy in uniform was scouring the building. Of course, we told him that he should get out, as this was ECMM property. After talking a little while, we found out that our landlord, Sevco, had abused him with a knife four years ago." Now Sevco was a Serb, was he not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "We saw the scars on his fingers, back and stomach. At that time he lived in Knin, and thus, had to flee. With the new situation he was back for a little revenge. Sevco is already in Belgrade which means he cannot get at him. Instead he ran amok a little with a hammer and was planning to burn down the building down. Sevco will never use the building again now as quite a lot of people are after him. Via his own restaurants he was a smuggler and a fence for stolen goods. He dealt in narcotics and was responsible for a lot of people being in prison. Not one of God's best efforts." Obviously, I'm just going through this. "And then he came back to exact his revenge because, of course -- from what had happened to him previously." But that is -- was your understanding?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He was there on a -- on a personal revenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But that was your understanding, sir, that that's the feeling that General Gotovina was touching upon during your interview on the 20th, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly this person had been a victim to the conduct of our landlord. And whether you can sanction the feelings of revenge is a different matter, and -- but absolutely, the psychology of being a victim was a predominant feature at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not saying sanctioning that conduct, sir, but you understand it.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me turn your attention to D799. This is -- we'll go through this quite briefly, and D799 is a daily monitoring activity for 20 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is an abbreviation of the conversation that you had with General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can scroll down just a bit on that page, in the English a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes that the second-to-last paragraph, the commander of the operative zone of Split, General Gotovina said to ECMM that: "Burning, looting, and harassment must be stopped by the police." But he added in regards "hatred towards an enemy who has burned, looted, and expelled one's families as a normal human reaction." Now, this was an abbreviation of your larger report, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is it not my report, but it may be contributions from some of the other persons in the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us turn to P893.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I'm looking at the clock and wondering what would be a good moment for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can just go now before we go into this document. That's quite all right. Or if you want me it continue, it's up to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And any further adjustment, more time or less time than expected?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I just give you a reading of that when I -- after the break, if that's possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will have a break, and we will resume at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now before we go into the next document which is P893, Mr. Hansen, the daily reports that you do, those are the factual reports as to what happened, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They are kind of the ground level from which everything else flows?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they feed into the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just show you P893.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this meeting that you went to with General Gotovina, you went with Mr. Leschly, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what was his role at the time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was head of the -- what is it called? The RC Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be the Regional Centre in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And he would be your superior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is his report of RC Zagreb, 17 to 23 September 1995. And on page 2 of this report at the bottom, it reflects Mr. Leschly's comments. The bottom page -- of the page. If we can just scroll -- yeah. Notes: "When Lieutenant-General Gotovina, commander of OZ Split was asked if he shared Zadar Zupanja`s opinion about the need for a state of emergency, in order ... to avoid the killings, lootings, and burnings, his only remark was 'what killings?' After which he went into an attack on the international community that had no right to 'moral slapping' of Croatia." Now, Mr. Hansen, this comment that Mr. Leschly puts in there about "what killings," comments attributed to General Gotovina about "what killings," and the next line, "no right to 'moral slapping' of Croatia." Those two comments are not reflected in your factual report, are they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. As you sit here, Mr. Hansen, those comments didn't happen during that meeting, did they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I mean, it would be unfair to say yes or no because I simply don't remember, and I certainly did not enter the phrases into my own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And had General Gotovina launched into some criticism or question that killings had taken place, that is a factual issue that you would normally have included in your report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now during the course of the time you were in ECMM, did you have a reason to question the objectivity of Mr. Leschly, when dealing with the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But for sure he had a -- a more colourful phrasing in his reports than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me take it one step further. Did you have occasion to question the objectivity of other ECMM report-writers during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about a guy by the name of Bent Jensen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Bent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you question his objectivity, sir?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would call him closer to the edge, and that he, at times, came across with preferences to one side of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know, Mr. Hansen, that the RSK intelligence services were trying to put people that work for the intelligence service into the ECMM as interpreters.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think all sides did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you likewise -- did you know they were trying to lie to the ECMM people, monitors in order to ascribe to the Serb position? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any particular recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me shift gears, and we're going go to Knin prior to Operation Storm. And I'd like to talk to you about a couple of issues that were raised by Mr. Hedaraly. And during direct examination you noted that had you been to the ARSK northern barracks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any recollection of the precise dates, but we were there, and -- in -- well, before the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's take it -- see if narrow it just a bit. Were you there prior to Milan Martic declaring a state of war in the RSK at the end of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, my recollection of this is that we were there before there was any -- anything developing in terms of -- of a major operation. So, yes, before the declaration of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if I can just take this one step further, Mr. Hansen. If you came to the area in May of 1995, would you tell the Trial Chamber that your meeting in -- no the northern bearings was earlier in time, in the May, possibly early June time-frame?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that would -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- now when you went there, did you arrive unannounced, or were you escorted by a member of the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we never arrived unannounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you went with, for instance, an ARSK liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were appointed meetings, and we -- whenever we met authorities no matter where, we always appointed meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Moving up to the time in -- prior to Operation Storm, in July, August of 1995, were you aware that the northern barracks was the headquarters for the 7th Krajina Corps of the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware -- were you there around the 4th or 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't know what troops were garrisoned there at the time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 2516, which is an ARSK document from the 7 Krajina corps command dated 27 July 1995. If you scroll up, this is an order 27 July 1995 from a Colonel Kozomara. If you just look at paragraph -- this is an order given to various entities within the ARSK 7th corps. "I hereby order -- collect people in SVK barracks (northern barracks, Benkovac barracks) conscripts who have their wartime assignment should be sent to their war units, and those who do not have a wartime assignment should be kept in the barracks and deployed as decided by the corps commander." Do you know anything about conscripts being gathered in the northern barracks towards the end of July?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 2516.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection from the Prosecution. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit D1278. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1278 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the Tvik factory. You noted for us during the course of your discussions with Mr. Hedaraly that you had been at the Tvik factory to conduct an economic survey of some fashion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went there on several occasions, in June and July and met with the manager and his management team on each of the occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you met with your management team -- excuse me the management team. Do you recall the gentleman's name that you met with?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a video, and I want to ask if you recognise any of the individuals in this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could, this would be D949. It's a RSK television clip from the 3rd of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it just to recognise persons?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just to recognise the person, but there is a question at the end that -- with regard to the dialogue that -- or the commentary that I would like to ask him about if he had a discussion about that dialogue, so it's a twofold purpose. Recognition and also a basis of a further question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have -- I have no French translation. Is there ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The transcript was sent this morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I think we have a standing procedure that one of the interpreters -- I hear from the French booth that they have not received a transcript of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My understanding from my court [sic] manager that a transcript was e-mailed this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, it is suggested that you now immediately send it by e-mail to the registrar who will then print it out for the interpreters, and perhaps meanwhile we could deal with another subject until this is all done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it is it coming now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but before it is printed and before it's distributed, that takes a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll go back to this film, Mr. Hansen. Let me address you to a different topic, and that would be in D950.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, D950. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is an information or document entitled "Information" from the Ministry of Defence for the RSK dated 10 July 1995, and it's signed by Mile Suput, the deputy minister, and its dates, as you said, 10 July, and I'm just reading the first paragraph: "Due to the urgent need of constructing lethal devices to be launched from an earth-bound rocket launcher and given the capacity of the Tvik factory, a Knin tool factory, we have allocated part of the production of certain products in cooperation with the Banja Metal factory, Dvor Na Uni to the aforementioned factory." Now, were you ever informed in July 10th after that or before that that the Tvik factory was assisting in making parts for lethal devices to be launched from an earth bound-rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your discussions with -- if they were in July or thereafter, in your discussions with the manager, he didn't tell you about it, nor did he tell you it was contemplated.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think is transcript is down, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do not know. I was listening to the French translation finishing your last words Mr. Kehoe. But apparently some other matter has upset you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that the transcript was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript was not running. Yes, the transcript is not running -- do we have any -- let me see whether it's just the transcript. No, we have -- the transcript is not running on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... LiveNote. I suggest that we proceed as we did before; that is, that we will continue, that we focus on the running transcript, and as soon as it brings us into problems, that we'll then stop. And that mean meanwhile, we ask the technicians to see whether we can get LiveNote running on the other system --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... as well. Then we could proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we're ready to go back to the video, if I'm not mistaken which would be D949.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do so, Mr. Kehoe, you put it to the witness whether he was aware that the Tvik factory was assisting in, et cetera, et cetera, which suggests that what we find in this document, which is already in evidence, of the 10th of July, that allocation means that it is all functioning already, which at least I have difficulties in understanding whether this is preparing for what has to happen. There are -- proposals are mentioned. So that is not entirely clear for me that the document tells us what you told the witness tells us, and I just want you to be aware that I'm still struggling with the document rather than being able to able to repeat what you said what it actually says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I have certainly read that into it, but maybe I just quote the actual document itself and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be probably are more expeditious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have asked the question whether he was informed, and then you included another element that it was assisting, or that it was ever -- I think you said a visit, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That seems to follow at least from the text of that document, so there I have no doubt in following you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can make this question as accurate as possible, and let me go back to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness doesn't know anything about it, and then, of course, and it appears that what he told us, that he had no idea, then of course to take him through the documents and to do the exegesis which, of course, the Chamber will have to do, but not necessarily a witness who doesn't know anything about it.
