Unless, Mr. Hansen, it's one of your hobbies in your spare time, but ... Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go back to the video. And again this is on the 3rd of September 1994, and I recognise that you weren't there. It's D949, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Speaker: Despite the four years of war and the imposed embargo, the state owned company Tvik from Knin has begun successfully resisting any hardship. The commander of the Serb army of the Krajina, Major-General Milan Celeketic, visited this company today along with his associates. "Reporter: As part of his regular activities of visiting commercial companies, the SVK commander Major-General Milan Celeketic accompanied by his logistics assistant Major-General Mrksic Bjelanovic and Colonel Dusan Smiljanic visited this morning the state owned company, the screw factory Tvik in Knin. While talking to the manager of this company, Mr. Jugslav Pavlovic, the commander was informed about the difficulties Tvik has been faced with under the conditions of war and the blockade on the international market. At the time of the war broke out, the Tvik factory had 3300 employees. This number was reduced to 2300 employees today of which more than 1.000 are conscript. Still, Tvik manages to fulfil any obligations towards the employees, the workers waiting to reassume their workplace and the conscripts. 50 per cent of the this company's production was designated for export, but today, it offers the cheapest product on the Yugoslav market. Mr. Pavlovic, the manager of Tvik, has assured the visitors that once the borders are reopened and export is possible again, this company could reassume regular business operations. General Celeketic and Mr. Pavlovic also discussed the military production programme in Tvik. After that, the commander and his associates visited the production facilities of this extremely important company."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, the gentleman at the Tvik factory that you went to talk about this economic survey, did you see him on this video at all?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember his appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall -- you don't recall his name?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a line in the -- this production, and again I understand it is September 1994 which reported that General Celeketic and Mr. Pavlovic also discussed the military production programme in Tvik. With the person that you spoke to that -- did he ever tell you that ever had been a military production programme at the Tvik factory?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What did he say on the contrary?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was an a nuts-and-bolts production that was halted because of no access to markets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us -- and I'm going to try to move through some topics briefly, Mr. Hansen, so if I'm going too fast --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the sake of the record and the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you are invited to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies to the Court and the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Hansen, when the shelling started at 5.00 a.m. in the morning, all the civilians that you were aware of went down to the basements of buildings, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you were in your residence for a period of time, and then you went over to the EU ECMM headquarters. Approximately what time was that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 9.00ish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were there from 9.00 until when?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the afternoon hours when we were evacuated by UN vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And approximately what time was that evacuation?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's -- it's about 3.00. But it is entered in my diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And from the time the shelling began until your evacuation by UN, those are the only two locations that you were in Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you got into the APC about 5.00 -- excuse me, about 3.00 you drove to UN Sector South, right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And while you were driving in this APC, you couldn't see anything, could you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, I guess other than the feet of the people who were driving the APC. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you leave any ECMM people behind when you got in the APC?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Affirmative. Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who did you leave behind?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was logistics staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall a name?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to your diary, and this is 1292 at tab 21, the first page. And it's, like, four paragraphs down. Do you see the paragraph starts: "The peace negotiations ..."?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can go to the hard copy if you want. I don't know if is easier. It's tab 21 in --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's coming now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just scroll down that a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see that second-to-last paragraph there, "The peace negotiations."

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And it says: "How things look in the town, we don't know. A patrol attempted to reach the Ministry of Defence but was stopped by hysterical, angry soldiers." Now you were not on that patrol, were you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know who was?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I do not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean -- whoever was on that patrol came back and informed you that they had run into hysterical and angry soldiers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another report, if I can, for the 5th, on D334.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could -- this is a sitrep of 12.45 on the 5th. If we can turn down to point 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The HV soldiers -- this is after the HV enters. "HV soldiers appear to professional and are treating the civilian population fairly. I'm not so sure about any soldiers they meet on their way through town, I saw three bodies that were not there on the way out. All of these were ARSK soldiers." I'd like you to compare that, sir, to Exhibit P1299, which is a report from the 7th of August, 1995. And if we could scroll down, talking about Knin, and this is on the 5th. As we move towards the -- you see that, says "a devastated Knin." You see that, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It says: "A devastated Knin with heavy infantry, and tank fighting was going on. About 30 dead bodies were seen on the street." Now, the report that we had from 12.45 the earlier day had three bodies, and when a summary report is put together two days later on the 7th, it is 30 bodies.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you account for that discrepancy, or is that accountable because of some of the anecdotal stores you might have received?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I cannot verify this information, and it is not my reporting, so -- so I would have no explanation to the inflation or to the difference in the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also note in your diary -- go back to page 3 of your diary. Again, 1292 at tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the second page of that document. I'm sorry, just the third page. This is all on the 5th. Just scroll up a bit, sir. Just a bit, yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is on the 5th, sir. And just going to that second paragraph, it notes -- and the time entry here, sir, is -- you have 10.00 a.m. That is what it has on the previous page, just to give you a little reference point. So there is a pause going on now. What is happening now, we don't know, but we use the pause to get our three colleagues to the HQ. It is risky driving through -- driving in the town, though. RSK soldiers are gradually retreating to the centre of town. They shoot at anything that moves, including us. They are panicky with nowhere to go." Now, did you observe this from the UN Sector South headquarters, that the RSK was moving towards the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean, I have -- I have no recollection of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, would you -- would someone have told you that this was going on?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You just don't recall?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we talked further about the fighting that was going on in Knin on the 5th, would you have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not because I was simply not travelling at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you note on this -- just to clear this up, if we go one page back to the 10.00 entry, the beginning of the 10.00 entry. It's about six lines down: "The real firing started at 5.00 this morning." Do you see that, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "The town was being completely hammered till about 9.00 a.m., then there was a pause before the shelling started again. The firing appears to be coming from the south, from Drnis area, and there is now direct fire." Do you know if that direct fire was coming from the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Today, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, just one last thing on this before we move on. You do know that -- or do you know that the HV units came in Knin from the north, not the south. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point, I don't think I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Fair enough. I'd like to talk to you a couple of things about some comments that you made in your statement beginning with your statement in 1995 that -- I do believe that Mr. Hedaraly went through with you, and that would be P1283 - thank you - on page 3, where you talk about the -- the shelling of Knin. Now, when you gave your statement or during this time or thereafter, did you realize what the situation, military situation, was between the HV/HVO forces and the joint Serb forces in Bihac? Did you have a knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early days of August, we did not have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So when you were looking at what was trying to be accomplished through Operation Storm, you -- that whole fact or what was going on with Bihac was not part of the equation. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. That could not be observed in any way from where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just talking about generally.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know that the Serbs were trying to take the Bihac pocket?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Bihac pocket is a story in its own right, and for sure, before, there had been attempts to take the pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you --

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have no recollection of -- of knowing at this particular time that the Serbs were trying to take the pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had they tried to take it in late July?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Looking at Operation Storm itself, as you sit here now, did you know what the breadth of Operation Storm was or how large an area it covered?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it would be fair to assume that it was about liberating the Serb-held territories of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the Serb-held territories in Croatia were in both Sector North and Sector South, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you understand that the attack in Operation Storm was an attack that went on in both Sector North and Sector South?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you likewise understand that the attack in Knin was an attempt by the HV to neutralize the ARSK headquarters that was located in Knin?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- and as a military man with military experience, sir?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Even as a reserve officer, you have a degree of military training?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You realize that taking or neutralizing the ARSK headquarters in Knin would jeopardize the entire ARSK operation throughout the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you likewise understand that this military operation was not an attempt to destroy Knin but to -- and the Krajina but to reintegrate it into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go to it item in here, you recognise that the damage from the shelling was minor?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note in your document that - if I can grab this here - what could be assessed to be -- this is on the fourth paragraph on page 3: "What could be assessed to be military targets, the ARSK headquarters, and the military bakery where it was not targeted." Do you mean barracks there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a bakery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where was the bakery; do you know?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere in downtown Knin. I mean, it was a facility that produced, well, bread for the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So as you sit here you have no knowledge that the headquarters of the ARSK was hit at 5.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you likewise know that the northern barracks and Senjak barracks were hit?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I'm not sure that I know it was not hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if -- if it was hit, I was still not having any -- I could not go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you learn thereafter that the Senjak barracks, the northern barracks, and the ARSK headquarters were all hit in the early morning hours of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after we were passing by, but see -- did not from where I was see any noticeable damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you go in?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, that -- let me withdraw that. As a man with a military background, you would understand that an attacking force would attempt to neutralize the communication capabilities of the ARSK, would they not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know whether the HV, beginning on the morning of the 4th, directed their artillery towards the communication capabilities for the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have -- I don't know, but it was -- I mean, if I was to assume, I would certainly assume that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In page 4 of your diary, which is the -- P1292, page 4, the third paragraph down, Sandra being your interpreter. You see: "Tells me ...."? "Sandra tells me about a friend, soldier friend, who was on the front line and couldn't understand why he wasn't getting any information through." When she told you that, did you take that to mean, sir, that there was in some fashion, a disruption of communication between soldiers in the front line and some type of command structure?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took that as a -- as an indication of a total breakdown of -- of both communication and line of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As you sit here today and you look at the attack on Knin, and what you learned, you now recognise, do you not, that this was more than any -- that this was a direct attack on a city that was subsequently followed by soldiers coming in and taking the area?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, could we ask the witness what he learned today and to what extent he is able to verify the accuracy of what has been put to him. For example, did he learn that there were three bodies or 30 bodies before we ask him an impression about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I'm not insisting on it. I'm, of course, to some extent, putting a footnote to your question because the witness is here not to obtain new knowledge and information. What we could ask him is whether what was put to him, which is not the same as what he learned, and it's my understanding that learning means learning what had happened, and that is, of course, a rather complex matter. But what was put to him, whether that in any way changes the opinion he had formed on the basis of his own observation on the assumption that was put to him is reliable information. Is that what you wanted to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, and ultimately, Mr. President -- and I will just put to him one last document on this score which is D389, which is the intelligence assessment by the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is -- just to show you, this is a report of the 4th of August, 1995. And the third, fourth paragraph down: "Knin was attacked from Livanjsko Polje from several directions, and by the time this information was drafted, between 200 and 300 rounds of different calibres impacted on the town. The first strike was carried out on the building of the SVK General Staff, which suffered great materiel damage with the fleet of vehicles almost completely destroyed. Later the fire was transferred on the military barracks 1300 kaplara, the Tvik factory, the railway intersection, residential buildings in the area beneath the Knin fortress, et cetera." Now, going back to Judge Orie's question, based on -- not only on what you learned, but what you learned from the 4th on to today, as the purpose of what happened during this attack, does that change your opinion, sir, as to what the shelling -- the purpose of the shelling was and the purpose of the attack on Knin on the 4th and 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no difference in opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us shift subjects, sir. And I'd like to talk to you a little bit looting that you discussed. And going through the -- some of the items, and I'll just pick out some items that we -- you talked about. And you talked about a collection point next to the UN base. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you also talked about the -- there being some looting going on with the individual soldiers in town. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me show you P805. You noted for us that you went out on the 7th of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we have a general situation at 2200 hours on the 7th, and it notes that: "Knin is now calm but with soldiers from the 4th and 7th Brigades still carrying out small-scale looting." Is that what you saw, sir, this small-scale looting as is reflected here by these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we saw looting, and I would certainly -- with the wisdom of hindsight, I would not call it small-scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's what was written at the time.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the two authors, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page. 5(b). If we can go -- excuse me, yeah, it's 5(b). "In Knin area it seems as if random looting and destruction of houses and property is about to reach a degree where it will get even more difficult to restart normal life here." Comment: "It is very unlikely that this is a deliberate policy of the authorities. It is more likely that as front line, more disciplined troops are moving out. The second-line soldiers are less disciplined and more ready to grab what they can." Now, again, that's an item that is done at the time by ECMM monitors that were there. Now, did you write -- did you review this report at the time?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is -- this report is written by the two gentlemen mentioned on the front page. And in a comment to -- to their assessment, I would say that this is it probably a fair assessment at the time of writing, which is on the 7th. And I would also subscribe to the assessment about the front line combat soldiers being changed or replaced by a different breed of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's as early as the 7th, according to this report?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'd like to talk to you about the organisational structure that you noted, and with the garage and trucks that were outside the UN facility? Now that you noted they were -- that various types of household goods, et cetera, TV sets, et cetera, were being brought to that location?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's truce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now do you have, Mr. Hansen, whether those particular items were being inventoried by the HV and put on a list?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if you -- you don't know that. Do you know whether the military police were seizing things and likewise inventorying things that they seized?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I ask you the same question for the civilian police. Do you know if they were, in fact, taking items or seizing items at check-points and putting them in -- in inventory?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, would you agree with me, sir, that knowledge about specific facts in that regard would be important in a determination by you or anyone else as to whether a person or group of people were looting or not?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the magnitude of -- of the looting would somehow, in my assessment at least, exclude the production of an inventory of merchandise being ferried out of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You say, sir, that because you have not seen an inventory; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I find it unlikely that it was a managed and -- operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. Now some of the -- you mention the going through Knin in town by the soldiers. Some of the going through houses and towns is done by a military in a clearing operation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's a normal operation that a military or police entity would do as they went through town?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to shift gears but still stay on looting. And I would like to talk to you about the waves. I mean, you said initially there was regular combat troops, and then soldiers came after that, and then civilians. And you noted for us that you believe that the civilians didn't begin to come back until your return in September. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time I saw them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's explore that a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to P933.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a sitrep of the 9th of August, 1995, in the -- right above military situation about a quarter of the way down: "It seems like Knin for the first time is becoming a big tourist attraction, extensive traffic was reported on the main road between Knin and Drnis." So civilians were, in fact, coming to the area as early as the 9th, according to the ECMM reporting. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is it right, and that is even my own report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next page. "We saw the same development in Drnis. A lot of civilians are in the city, and it seems they are looking for property that belonged to them previously." So, Mr. Hansen, what you're reporting is that civilians are there on the 9th, and they believed that they have been victimised and that property has been stolen, so they're going into other houses, such as Serb houses, and taking back what is theirs. Is that an accurate assessment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Objection. That mischaracterizes the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's take it, then, one by one. Is your report about civilians that are there on the 9th, Mr, Hansen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is your report about civilians that are there on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that is my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is the report about civilians that believed that they had been victimised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that their property was stolen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding of this paragraph is that they are looking for property that belonged to them previously, property that may have been destroyed or -- I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Their own property or property left behind by others or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this particular instance, it is property left behind by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you were asked whether you reported about property stolen, that you say it was -- perhaps was their property stolen, but what they were taking back, might not have been their own. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just staying with this, would this people who were taking property that they believed belonged to them, or taking property that -- just to furnish their house that was empty, or both?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have no method to -- to make a direct correlation between a person and a property and establish ownership. And what we saw as a general feature was that houses and apartments were broken into and household items were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to P1289, which is another sitrep that I believe is yours, sir, from the 12th of September, 1995. And maybe we can put a little bit more flesh on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go down to the end of paragraph 2. Right there. Right above human rights monitoring. "The readiness of the local authorities to receive DPs from the coast and individuals visiting Knin moving into houses and furnishing their new homes by looting neighbouring houses." So just staying with that, that was part of this too. People going and just looting an empty house next door and bringing it into their house, be they displaced people, or whatever. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just going back with this, Mr. Hansen. These civilians came back almost right after the end of Operation Storm, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn out attention to -- to some of the items concerning the burning, and I would like to just go through a couple of incidents with you about this. Because you -- you said some items -- some items with regard to this burning, you appear to say were organised. And I would like to turn your attention to P933. And P933, going to the military situation, and this is dated the 9th of August, 1995: "In Biskupija five troops with a white Lada and a green Land Rover were burning houses. It was obvious that they were surprised to see us." Now, first of all, the Lada and the green Land Rover, did you get a HV plate from this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume not, as it is not entered in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And these were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And these were five individuals that were dressed in camouflage uniforms, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, it notes in here that the -- "from the badges, we know they belongings to Diverzantia, a special unit with skull insignia. The unit is attached to the 7th Brigade." Now, where did you get the information that this Diverzantia was connected to the 7th Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today I have really no additional comment to -- to this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, did you ever come to learn, sir, that there is no unit or section that is part of the HV that has a skull and cross bones or is called Diverzantia?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have learned that later, but at this the of writing, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you now know that Diverzantia is not part of the HV?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, was this a, like a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn your attention to another entity -- another incident. And that is this incident, I believe, that was discussed with Mr. Hedaraly at P830, which is this incident in Kosovo. This is a sitrep, P830 is a sitrep for 10 August 1995. If we go to page 2, towards the bottom of page 2, if we can scroll down a bit. We -- we have the reporting on this Kosovo incident: "In Kosovo six uniformed soldiers were seen going from house to house setting fires." You talked about that during the course of your testimony on direct. Now, if we look at P1290, which is your comprehensive report, you report on this ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we go to page 6 of this document. If we can go -- just scroll down toward the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in Kosovo -- do you see the bottom there, Mr. Hansen?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You report: "Six uniformed HV soldiers were wearing no unit sign. They were supported by HV pick-ups." So what we have is a -- six individuals that were wearing camouflage uniforms; right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Other than the camouflage uniforms, there's no indication that they were part of the HV or operating as part of an HV unit, to accomplish a specific task, was there?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot get that any closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the units that you saw out there, I mean we have six here, there's six soldiers in this Kosovo entry. I mean, you never saw any soldiers in groups larger than six doing anything like burning, did you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. They were always in small numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And you never saw that, while they were doing this, some overall commander and some officer directing them to do A, B, and C, did you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the next issue that we want to talk about just briefly, and -- I mean, is -- when we look at this burning, I mean, you realize, do you not -- and let me just give you a reference point. Let's go to P934. If we can to the second page under humanitarian/human rights matters: "In A, team Split had a meeting with secretary of Split Zupanija DP's association today. They were informed that there were 200.000 displaced people in Croatia at the moment, of which the secretary hoped half would be returning home to the newly freed territories within the next three months." So, Mr. Hansen, what we're talking about is approximately 100.000 displaced people coming back to the Krajina. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the information here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And they would -- these displaced people would be coming back to not only the cities but to the countryside as well. Weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, prior to Operation Storm when you drove through the Krajina, you saw scores of burnt out houses, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was in the rural countryside as well as in and around cities.

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you concluded, did you not, that these houses in the rural countrysides that had been burnt prior to Operation Storm were Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- now based on that, as you sit here, Mr. Hansen, you can conclude that at least some percentage of these displaced people that were out at the coast, this 100.000, were going to come back to the Krajina and some were going to live in the country side, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me take you through a couple of these documents. And go to P935. I'm going read you a couple of items together, and we can come to one last conclusion. P935 is a sitrep of 13th of August, 1995, of ECMM. If we can go to this third page, bottom of the third page. Right before the end of the page: "Displaced people from hotels, caravan sites, along the coast, and refugees from western Europe have been seeping back to visit their original homes and some to stay [sic]. Representative of Split Zupanja DP's association estimates that 100.000 DP's will return to the free territories." If we can turn to P2156. This is a document that was referred to by Mr. Hedaraly. Page 3. I'm just going to go through these, reference these, Mr. Hansen, so you can take a look at them, and I will ask you a couple of questions in the interests of speed. This is a daily monitoring report for 11/13th August. If we can go to page 3. It notes in the centre of the page about how it is going to be a staged return of displaced people back to the Krajina. If we can go to P511. P511. This is 18 August. Sitrep of 18 August. If we go to the last page, economic and infrastructure. "Today the rain and sheer lack of unburned houses meant that very few fires were observed. The fields are still left with nobody working in them. How the Croatians will harvest the crops is not yet known, and it seems to become a large problem. Or will they just let it rot [sic] in the fields? Will the DP become forced labour in the fields?" Next one, P3 -- 937. This is a sitrep of the 20th of August, 1995. If we can go to the last page of P937. Paragraph (d) there: "DPs and refugees from Croatia and Europe are filtering back into the area. However, no infrastructure and destroyed houses makes immediate habitation impossible ..." P812, first page is sitrep, 23 August 1995, and they're talking about Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we just scroll down a bit on that front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "The plan for Benkovac," B being Benkovac, "is to serve as an accommodation to DPs coming from the tourist areas. These will be accommodated in tents, if necessary." And the last one we'll talk about before we get into it, this P953. And this is it a sitrep from 9 October 1995. If we go to the last page. And interestingly it is an economic survey going back to the Tvik factory. And there is discussions with the manager at Tvik, and then the comment at the end: "Housing problem is paramount. Nobody will come to work without this problem solved." So we can go through more of these, Mr. Hansen, but do you see what the problem is: There is burning of houses going on that you have reported, and there's an inability to bring displaced people back into the area because of the burnt houses, and they can't begin to work. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is at a time when the Republic of Croatia is trying to get the Krajina back on its feet economically and get the displaced people away from the coast and back into their area. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that was the overriding intent of the Republic of Croatia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now with that intent, you understand that permitting people to burn these house would essentially cut the legs off that entire plan to bring all those people back to the Krajina, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: STIG MARKER HANSEN [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to deliver a decision, which is an oral decision on the admission into evidence of P1072, P1073, and P1074. Documents that were, until now, marked for identification. On the 3rd of November 2008, the Prosecution informed the Chamber and the Defence that in the course of Zeljko Zganjer's testimony, it would seek to admit into evidence, inter alia, three documents dated the 25th of October, 1995, relating to investigations carried out on the alleged killings in Gosici, Varivode, and the area of Zrmanja. On the 12th of November, Zeljko Zganjer was cross-examined by the Gotovina Defence on these documents at transcript pages 11658 to 11659. The Defence advanced that the numbering on the documents originating from the criminal military police was not sequential, thus suggesting that they were fabricated. Zeljko Zganjer was unable to give a explanation on the matter as he did not know how the documents were numbered. At transcript pages 11661 to 662, the Prosecution objected to the Defence`s suggestion that the documents were fabricated. The Prosecution further argued that the Defence should have questioned Damir Simic, the author of P1072 and P1073, and witness to these proceedings on the authenticity of the documents. Under Rule 89(C), the Chamber may admitted into evidence any document that is relevant and probative. P1072 is an operative plan signed by the criminal military police official Damir Simic in respect of the Zadar's district state attorney's request to conduct investigations into the alleged killings in Gosici Varivode, and the area of Zrmanja. The work plan indicates that by 8.00 a.m. on the 25th October, 1995, the addresses of certain suspects had to be asserted. P1073, also dated the 25 October, 1995, is an arrest warrant for two of the suspects. The arrest warrant contains the addresses of two of the suspects. P1074 is a search warrant dated the 25th of October, 1995, for one of the suspects's living quarters. The search warrant also mentioned this suspect's address. P1072, P1073, and P1074 are relevant to Counts 1, 6, and 7 of the indictment; that is, the charges of persecution and murder. The Chamber notes that the P1073 and P1074 carry the document numbers ending with 45 and 46, respectively. And that P1072 carries a document number ending with 51. The numbering on the documents suggest that P1072 was written after P1073 and P1074. However, P1072, which was issued on the same date as the two other documents, indicates that, by 8.00 a.m., on the 25th of October, 1995, the addresses of certain suspects still needed to be ascertained; whereas, P1073 and P1074, which expressly cite a suspect's address, indicate that this address had already been ascertained by the time P1072 was written. The Chamber observes that it could well be that the documents were numbered at a later stage, much after they were written, and that the officer in charge of the numbering simply numbered P1073 and P1074 before he or she numbered P1072. The Chamber further notes that all documents tendered have been signed, and two of them have been stamped. Considering this, and having no further indication as to the documents' lack of authenticity, the Chamber finds that P1072, P1073, and P1074 are probative and admits them into evidence. The Chamber will take into consideration the arguments raised by the Defence when ultimately assessing the wait to be attributed to these documents. The Chamber requests that the Registrar change the status of these documents in e-court accordingly; that is, instead of MFIed, admitted into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. The next -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next issues are the submissions on the five questions. The Prosecution has given an answer to the first question, more or less, by giving a schedule for the witnesses to be called. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will certainly assist you in making this hope coming into fulfilment, Mr. Hedaraly. That's an answer to the first question of the five questions that were put to the parties on the 15th of January. We meanwhile received a written submission which I will put on the record, but just by reading it, Mr. Cayley, you are answered on behalf of all of the Defence teams, although you left it open that this joint submission could be followed by more specific submissions by each of the Defence teams. The answer to question 2 was that the Defence would need one Court day for each team for Rule 98 bis submissions. The answer to question 3 was that the Defence would need 20 working days after the end of the OTP case to the Rule of 98 bis submissions, so in order to prepare for these submissions. The answer to question 4 was that the Defence teams would need 60 working days between the Rule 98 bis submissions and the commencement of the Defence case. And the answer to the fifth question was that the Defence cases would go in the order of the accused on the indictment. Before I give an opportunity to the parties to add anything, let me be very clear. The Chamber has considered the answers, does not give a final ruling on the matter; that would be too early. But as matters stand now, thought that it might assist the Defence to receive from the Chamber, and most likely you will receive it from one minute from now on your e-mail, a statistical analysis, I think, of the last 10 to 12 cases and invites the Defence to come up with more realistic plans. If you look at them, you'll see that often five, six, seven days between the close of the case and -- we're not blind and deaf. For special circumstances, of course, some of the -- what happened in previous cases was also influenced by very special circumstances. Sometimes a long period of time was including, for example, a recess. But the Chamber is not heading for final Scheduling Order which would bring the start of the Defence cases almost beyond the summer recess. That is not something that the Chamber is seriously considering at this moment. So the Defence is invited to -- first of all, to read the e-mail that will be sent by the legal officer of the Chamber, and then to come back with other suggestions. I don't think at this moment there is any further need -- of course, if you like to add something to your new suggestions or point at specific circumstances, then, of course, the Chamber will take notice of that. Then, Mr. Misetic, I would like to give you an opportunity, but in private session, to raise a matter you said you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Although I intended to deal with a few outstanding MFI matters, I will not do that because time is too short. I again apologise for the interpreters, transcribers, but also I'm aware that security and others are also affected by this. The parties should keep themselves ready to deal with the MFI issues where I said responses by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just because it is related to the witness, Mr. President, the diary, I don't know if there is a decision. We can wait till Monday. But if there is one, if we could just -- now that the witness is gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the witness -- to admit it or not? We'll do that, whether he is gone or not. I mean, it's there, you -- there are no submissions, Mr. Kehoe, in relation to the way in which it was transcribed. Then we'll deal that as well on Monday briefly. I take it that the MFI list will need another ten minutes of attention at this moment. We adjourn, and we'll resume on Monday, 26th of January, 9.00, in the morning, Courtroom II.
